expectations.text: Identifies the fat controller / missing service layer anti-pattern
expectations.evidence: The billing module, as shipped, is a textbook example of the Fat Controller anti-pattern. Every route handler in routes.ts performs direct database access, calls the Stripe API directly, implements business logic, and manages state transitions — all without a service layer, a repository, or any domain abstraction.

expectations.text: Notes that business logic (computing daysLeft, isActive, customer lookup) is embedded in route handlers
expectations.evidence: GET /billing/subscription — retrieves the local subscription record, then calls stripe.subscriptions.retrieve(), computes daysLeft, derives isActive, and extracts planName. This is application-layer orchestration and domain computation sitting in the route handler.

expectations.text: Flags direct Stripe API calls in route handlers instead of an application/infrastructure layer
expectations.evidence: GET /billing/portal — the simplest handler but still makes a direct Stripe API call inside the route. Also: Infrastructure clients belong in the infrastructure layer, constructed by the Container (composition root), not hardcoded in the presentation layer.

expectations.text: Flags direct DB queries (db.select, db.update) in route handlers
expectations.evidence: routes.ts imports directly from the database layer: import { eq, and, desc } from 'drizzle-orm'; import { db } from '../../db'; import { subscriptions, invoices, users } from '../../db/schema'; Per the dependency rule, routes.ts must never import from drizzle-orm or ../../db/schema.

expectations.text: Recommends extracting a BillingService (application layer) and/or BillingRepository (infrastructure layer)
expectations.evidence: Priority 1 (Critical): Create BillingService — extract all use-case logic out of route handlers. Priority 2 (Critical): Create BillingRepository — extract all Drizzle queries into one class. Also includes a full code sample for BillingService class and BillingRepository interface.

expectations.text: Notes the missing composition root / dependency injection
expectations.evidence: Infrastructure clients belong in the infrastructure layer, constructed by the Container (composition root), not hardcoded in the presentation layer. The service.ts code sample shows: constructor(private repo: BillingRepository, private stripe: StripeClient, private secrets: SecretsProvider) and the refactored route uses await getContext(app.container, req).
